result.rationale: The diff shows `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` replaced by `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which inverts the slug condition: previously slug was set only when team billing was disabled; now it is set only when enabled, while requestedSlug still gated on IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED. The two conditions are no longer the intended either/or, changing behavior for both self-hosted and billing deployments in the manner described.

judged_text: The slug spread condition is inverted: `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` replaces the original `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, while the paired requestedSlug line keeps its original billing-enabled gating, so the two conditions no longer form the intended either/or. On billing-disabled (self-hosted) deployments organizations are now created with neither slug nor requestedSlug (previously slug), leaving the org without a working URL; on billing-enabled deployments the slug is assigned at creation time (previously only metadata.requestedSlug until payment), bypassing the team-billing gate.
